ab: Abkhaz needs its own extended Cyrillic alphabet and multigraph repertoire; use a named non-Slavic table, not Russian pronunciation rules.
av: Avar includes extended letters and multigraph combinations; pin the Avar alphabet/version and longest-match behavior.
ba: Bashkir-specific Cyrillic letters need explicit entries; select the chosen Bashkir Latin standard rather than borrowing Tatar or Russian outputs.
be: Belarusian practical schemes and ISO-style scholarly transliteration differ; specify the selected scheme and treatment of the apostrophe/soft sign.
bg: Bulgarian needs a selected national/practical or scholarly table; letters such as hard sign and digraph outputs must follow that scheme.
bua: Buryat needs extended Cyrillic vowel/consonant entries and alphabet-version policy; bounded spelling conversion is table-driven.
ce: Chechen multigraphs and extended letters require language-aware matching; a generic Russian table is incomplete.
cv: Chuvash-specific Cyrillic characters and combining equivalents need their own table; preserve distinctions under the selected standard.
crh: Crimean Tatar has separately listed Cyrillic and Latin variants. Use script detection and a named conversion table; alphabet conversion is not a pronunciation model.
kk: Kazakh has multiple historical/proposed Latin conventions. Version the selected table and support its extra Cyrillic letters; do not promise an unspecified universal Latin spelling.
kv: Komi needs the appropriate Cyrillic alphabet/version and language-specific extensions; no learned model is implied for orthographic output.
ky: Kyrgyz-specific vowels and nasal consonant need explicit mappings; legacy Latin conventions should be separately selectable.
mk: Macedonian uses its own Cyrillic letters and practical conventions; a small language-specific map is sufficient for standard spelling romanization.
chm: Meadow Mari requires extended Cyrillic vowel entries. Keep other Mari varieties outside this code's pronunciation promise.
mn: Cyrillic Mongolian and traditional Mongolian are distinct input profiles; a Latin table for Cyrillic does not implement traditional-script reading.
os: Ossetian includes its own Cyrillic inventory, including the ae letter; use an Ossetian table and make ASCII folding an explicit lossy option.
ru: Russian spelling romanization is rule/table-driven. Recovering an omitted yo distinction, stress or conventional personal-name spelling may require lexical information.
sr: Select Cyrillic-to-Latin conversion or preserve Latin spelling according to the actual script. Reverse Latin digraphs can be ambiguous at letter boundaries.
tg: Tajik uses Persian-derived vocabulary but Cyrillic spelling; its extra letters need a Tajik map. This is not the same task as vowel recovery from Persian script.
tt: Tatar Cyrillic and Latin conventions need distinct profiles. Verify the input script rather than inferring it solely from a translation/OCR table label.
tyv: Tuvan uses extended Cyrillic letters; a named non-Slavic table is a bounded target, while pronunciation/name preference remains a separate feature.
udm: Udmurt-specific Cyrillic and combining variants need explicit mappings; avoid silently collapsing distinctions in a generic Slavic transform.
uk: Ukrainian letters and word-position rules differ from Russian. Choose a Ukrainian scheme; preserve proper-name overrides separately.
sah: Yakut/Sakha needs its own extended Cyrillic inventory and combination rules; baseline romanization can use a small table with finite rules.
ar: Unvowelled Arabic supports several lexical readings. Expose consonantal spelling and inferred-pronunciation modes; select dialect/standard and allow name overrides.
bal: Baluchi/Balochi has regional orthographies. The catalog default is Arabic-derived; choose a variety and a vowel policy before training a pronunciation model.
fa-AF: Dari is stored under original fa-AF/prs vendor codes. Use Dari-specific readings and names even where its Persian-derived script mapper is shared.
ks: Kashmiri Arabic-derived writing uses language-specific letters and vowel marks; optional/omitted marks and other scripts need explicit handling and lexical validation.
ckb: Sorani writes most vowels, but short i is often unwritten. Use rule-first spelling conversion and optional lexical recovery for that missing-vowel case. Azure's literal ku means Sorani; Google's ku means Kurmanji.
ms-Arab: Jawi-to-Rumi should recover standard Malay words, including omitted-vowel choices, rather than emit generic Arabic letter names.
ps: Pashto has extended letters and dialect-sensitive readings; spelling conversion is bounded, while inferred short vowels and names need a Pashto lexical layer.
fa: Persian short vowels are commonly omitted; readable forms require lexical/contextual readings. Written transliteration can remain deterministic under a named Persian scheme.
pa-PK: CLDR's default-script inference for Google's Pakistan Punjabi variant is Arabic-derived/Shahmukhi; this is not an explicit provider input-script guarantee. Keep the route distinct from Gurmukhi Punjabi and use Punjabi-specific lexical readings.
pa-Arab: Shahmukhi Punjabi has omitted-vowel ambiguity. Share low-level Arabic-script parsing, then apply Punjabi word readings and the chosen Latin convention.
sd: Sindhi's extended Perso-Arabic inventory must be mapped explicitly. Select Arabic versus Devanagari input and do not borrow Urdu pronunciation wholesale.
ur: Urdu needs Urdu-specific letters, word readings and vowel recovery for readable output; a literal spelling profile can preserve only the information present.
ug: Uyghur's modern Arabic alphabet writes vowels explicitly. Start with its alphabet/positional-vowel rules; routine Arabic-style full vowel restoration is unnecessary for that bounded script conversion.
hy: Armenian Eastern/Western pronunciation and legacy/reformed orthography can differ; the language code alone does not select a spoken convention.
ka: Georgian letter-to-string conversion is compact and deterministic once the scheme is chosen; preserve ejective markers and handle uppercase/legacy forms deliberately.
el: Greek practical romanization may need neighboring-letter/digraph rules. State Modern versus Ancient and the named convention.
he: Pointed Hebrew provides more reading information than unpointed text. A spelling mapper must not silently invent vowels for an unpointed word.
yi: Use Yiddish-specific digraph/pointing rules under the selected standard; narrow exceptions such as traditionally Hebrew-spelled forenames may need a dictionary. Do not require a lexicon for every Hebrew-derived word.
as: Assamese and Bengali share the script but not all letters/readings. Use Assamese-specific inventory and vowel/phonology rules after a shared structural parser.
bn: Bengali structural transliteration is algorithmic; conventional spoken romanization requires Bengali inherent-vowel and lexical-reading choices.
awa: Awadhi can reuse a Devanagari structural parser, but its pronunciation rules must be validated separately from Hindi.
bho: Bhojpuri needs its own inherent-vowel/word-reading policy; a Devanagari spelling output is the low-risk bounded baseline.
brx: Bodo's catalog default is Devanagari and can use a structural script mapper. Hindi schwa deletion is not evidence of correct Bodo pronunciation; validate Bodo-specific rules.
hne: Chhattisgarhi shares Devanagari structure with Hindi but requires language-specific word readings and vowel behavior for pronunciation output.
doi: Dogri is Devanagari-primary here, with Takri/Arabic alternatives in CLDR metadata. Orthographic conversion can share a parser; actual alternate-script input needs another profile.
hi: Hindi readable romanization needs schwa deletion and exceptions/morphology; full inherent-vowel spelling transliteration is a separate algorithmic mode.
gom: Konkani has several writing traditions. This catalog's default is Devanagari; choose a language/orthography standard and validate pronunciation independently of Marathi.
mai: Maithili is Devanagari-primary here, with historical Tirhuta alternatives. A readable engine needs Maithili-specific vowel/readings data.
mr: Marathi has its own vowels, consonant inventory and inherent-vowel conventions; reuse Devanagari parsing, not Hindi pronunciation rules.
mwr: Marwari/Marwadi uses several orthographies; CLDR default Devanagari is a routing assumption. Choose the actual script and variety before guaranteeing pronunciation.
new: Nepalbhasa/Newari is Devanagari-primary in this catalog but has other script traditions. Its phonology must not be replaced by a Nepali reading model.
ne: Nepali requires its own schwa/word-reading policy. A shared Devanagari transducer is only the structural first stage.
sa: IAST-style Sanskrit transliteration can follow written consonants, vowels and conjuncts algorithmically. Word segmentation/sandhi analysis should be optional features.
gu: Gujarati has dependent vowels and inherent-vowel behavior; reliable readable forms require Gujarati rules and lexical exceptions.
pa: Gurmukhi Punjabi needs vowel-sign, nasalization, gemination and tone-related conventions under the selected scheme; its pipeline differs from Shahmukhi.
kn: Kannada standard orthographic romanization is a structural rule problem; pronunciation refinements and name conventions should be separately evaluated.
tcy: Tulu is Kannada-script-primary under CLDR here. Use Tulu-specific readings; Tulu-Tigalari or other input scripts require separate support rather than a Kannada-language model.
ml: Malayalam needs consonant-vowel state, conjunct/chillu handling and orthographic-version normalization. Conservative spelling romanization is rule-first.
or: Odia/Oriya requires its own syllable parser and vowel rules; alphabetic substitution is insufficient even when no learned model is needed for a named spelling scheme.
ta: Tamil orthographic transliteration can be deterministic; pronunciation-oriented voicing/allophones and loanwords need Tamil-specific context and exceptions.
te: Telugu standard spelling romanization can use syllable/vowel rules; a learned model is optional for measured pronunciation exceptions.
si: Sinhala has inherent-vowel and dependent-sign structure; use a Sinhala-specific table/rule engine, not an unmodified Sanskrit/Hindi parser.
am: Amharic Ethiopic syllable mapping can be compact. Sixth-order vowel interpretation and unmarked gemination limit a full pronunciation guarantee.
ti: Tigrinya needs its own Ethiopic reading/convention profile. Shared syllabic code points do not justify Amharic word readings.
zh: Require the reading language/profile; if the caller chooses Mandarin, use phrase/polyphone processing and Hanyu Pinyin. A Han script tag alone is insufficient.
zh-CN: For an explicitly selected Mandarin profile use Hanyu Pinyin with polyphone/phrase readings. Simplified script does not remove reading ambiguity.
zh-Hans: Select Mandarin or another reading language explicitly; then use its lexicon/context model. Simplified/traditional conversion is a separate phrase-sensitive task.
zh-TW: For a Mandarin/Taiwan profile use Mandarin lexical readings and selected regional/naming conventions. Traditional script is not a pronunciation specification.
zh-Hant: Traditional characters may represent different languages. Choose the language and romanization scheme before selecting readings.
zh-HK: Hong Kong locale is not proof of a unique pronunciation language. Offer explicit Cantonese/Jyutping versus Mandarin/Pinyin profiles.
lzh: Literary Chinese requires a declared reading tradition (for example modern Mandarin reading versus another tradition); a generic Han character table cannot make that choice.
yue: Cantonese requires Cantonese lexical readings and a named scheme such as Jyutping; Mandarin Pinyin data is inappropriate.
ja: Kana alone is algorithmic; Kanji words and names need lexical/morphological readings before Hepburn or another selected renderer. The current government guidance changed in December 2025; version naming rules.
ko: Hangul needs syllable decomposition and standard-specific sound-change rules. Hanja needs lexical readings, and personal names may use conventional spellings.
th: Readable RTGS needs word/syllable identification and pronunciation knowledge, including silent letters. Compare lexicon/rule and small neural baselines.
lo: Use Lao-specific syllable and initial/final rules with a lexical exception layer where needed; orthographic ALA-LC and readable-name conventions are different targets.
km: Khmer consonant series/register affects vowel readings. Parse orthographic clusters and add lexical readings/segmentation for pronunciation output.
my: Burmese spelling romanization can follow a named scheme; spoken-style reading needs lexical/contextual processing. Legacy Zawgyi conversion is a separate concern.
shn: Shan ALA-LC spelling romanization is rule-first: inherent vowel, syllable boundaries and tone/final marks. Do not apply Burmese pronunciation to Shan text.
bo: Tibetan Wylie is a stack-aware spelling representation; an extended Wylie output scheme must be specified separately. A modern spoken reading requires dialect and lexical/phonological processing.
dz: Dzongkha needs its own Roman Dzongkha/readable convention; Tibetan Wylie spelling is not a substitute for Dzongkha pronunciation.
mn-Mong: Traditional Mongolian requires positional/variant processing and, for conventional lexical readings, vowel-harmony/context/dictionary information. Keep it separate from Cyrillic Mongolian.
iu-Cans: Inuktut/Inuktitut syllabics need syllable-to-string and final/length rules with regional selection. Latin input has its own identity path.
dv: Thaana uses written vowel signs and sukun; combine them with base letters and apply Dhivehi-specific positional rules.
mni-Mtei: Meitei Mayek uses dependent signs and distinct final forms. Azure's unqualified mni transliteration metadata identifies Mtei; Bengali-script Meitei is a separate profile.
sat-Olck: Ol Chiki is alphabetic, with modifiers, rather than a Devanagari-style abugida. Apply a Santali-specific Latin scheme.
bm-Nkoo: The vendor label NKo refers to a script-based Manding catalog entry; apply a declared language/romanization policy and preserve tone/length distinctions as required.
ber-Tfng: Use a named Tifinagh/Tamazight table and variety scope; do not imply every Amazigh variety has identical alphabet/romanization conventions.
tlh-Piqd: Require the declared pIqaD glyph encoding/font convention. The conversion is table-driven only after that choice; no listed Azure transliteration pair was found for this script.
de: German is already Latin. If ASCII folding is requested, expose a policy such as umlaut digraphs versus accent removal and explicit sharp-s handling.
tr: Turkish is already Latin. Locale-aware casing must preserve dotted/dotless I distinctions before any optional ASCII folding.
az: Azerbaijani defaults to Latin here, but Arabic/Cyrillic inputs need distinct profiles; dotted/dotless I and other letters need locale-aware handling.
vi: Vietnamese is already Latin. Preserve tone/vowel marks for normal spelling; an ASCII slug requires explicitly lossy accent and stroked-letter handling.
yo: Yoruba is already Latin. Tone and underdot distinctions should be preserved unless the caller explicitly requests lossy ASCII output.
ig: Igbo is already Latin; preserve its vowel/consonant marks where the output format allows them.
haw: Hawaiian is already Latin. Okina and macrons are spelling distinctions; deleting punctuation/marks is an explicit slug policy.
mi: Maori is already Latin. Preserve macrons in normal spelling, with a separate documented ASCII mode.
to: Tongan is already Latin; glottal-stop and vowel-length marks require a deliberate preservation/folding policy.
sm: Samoan is already Latin; retain glottal-stop and vowel-length notation when present.
ty: Tahitian is already Latin; apostrophe/glottal and vowel-length handling belongs to spelling/slug policy.
uz: Uzbek is Latin-primary here; apostrophe-like letters/marks must be normalized deliberately. Cyrillic and Arabic Uzbek require separate input profiles.
tk: Turkmen is Latin-primary here; Cyrillic/Arabic variants need separate mapping tables and script detection.
ff: Fulani/Fula is Latin-primary in the catalog. Adlam is an additional writing system and must not be silently passed through a Latin-only route.
ha: Hausa is Latin-primary here, with Ajami alternatives; dotted/hooked Latin letters and Arabic-derived inputs require different handling.
jv: Javanese is Latin-primary in this catalog. Javanese-script text needs a separate abugida parser and language rules.
su: Sundanese is Latin-primary here; native Sundanese-script input requires a separate structural transform.
ban: Balinese is Latin-primary here; Balinese-script input requires a separate consonant/vowel/cluster parser.
bbc: Batak Toba is Latin-primary here; Batak-script input requires a separate syllabic/abugida transform.
mak: Makassar is Latin-primary here; Lontara/Buginese-family input has a different spelling/reading problem and must be separately specified.
hmn: Google's generic Hmong label is Latin-primary under CLDR here. Hmong Daw mww and non-Latin Hmong scripts are distinct scopes.
mww-Latn: Azure documentation explicitly labels Hmong Daw Latin; this overrides the different CLDR likely script for unqualified mww. Original vendor code remains mww.
trp: Kokborok is Latin-primary under CLDR here. Its being an Indic-region language does not imply Devanagari or Bengali input; route by the actual script.
ms: Malay is Latin-primary here. Jawi is separately listed as ms-Arab and requires a different lexical conversion path.
kmr: Kurmanji is Latin-primary in this catalog. Google's literal ku is normalized to this northern Kurdish entry; Azure's literal ku is Sorani and is kept separate.
iu-Latn: Inuktut/Inuktitut already in Latin needs preservation, not syllabic conversion. Select the regional orthography for optional normalization.
sat-Latn: Santali already written in Latin needs preservation. Ol Chiki and other scripts need separate transformations.
ber-Latn: Latin Tamazight needs preservation and optional mark policy; the Tifinagh entry is assessed separately.
bs-Cyrl: Bosnian Cyrillic can use a standard Bosnian/Serbo-Croatian script conversion; the Latin entry needs no romanization.
bs: Bosnian is Latin-primary here; the separately listed Cyrillic variant needs a different conversion route.
sr-Latn: Serbian already in Latin needs preservation. Latin-to-Cyrillic is another direction and may require care with digraph boundaries.
tlh-Latn: Klingon's designed Latin orthography has meaningful case and apostrophes; a generic lowercasing slug policy loses information.
en: English is already Latin. Converting English spelling to pronunciation is a separate G2P task and should not be added to romanization.
no: Google's generic Norwegian code is retained separately from Azure/Google Bokmal nb; both are Latin and need no romanization.
nb: Norwegian Bokmal is Latin; normalize existing spelling rather than treating it as a phonetic conversion task.
pt: Generic Portuguese and Brazil/Portugal regional entries remain separate catalog keys. All use the same identity-first Latin approach.
pt-BR: Brazilian Portuguese is already Latin. Regional translation support does not imply a distinct transliteration model.
pt-PT: European Portuguese is already Latin; preserve its spelling and expose ASCII folding separately.
mni: The selected Meitei script matters more than the unqualified language label; never silently substitute Bengali-language pronunciation.
